_readme: Moody Center (MCA), 2001 Robert Dedman Drive - Gensler's 2022 arena, as data for js/slopes-apartments.js (schema: docs/apartments.md). NOT an apartment: it is here because the owner asked for its exterior to be right. Every number carries a _src naming a source in `sources`, or says derived or unknown. Metres in the footprint's oriented bounding box: L=148.45 W=121.44, +u at bearing 135.5 deg, so u=0 is the NORTH-WEST end, +u runs south-east, v=0 is the SOUTH-WEST edge and +v runs north-east.
name: Moody Center

sources.S1: OSM way 953200132 (Overpass, 2026-09-06): building=stadium, name 'Moody Center', ref MCA, architect=Gensler, start_date 2022-04-18, addr 2001 Robert Dedman Drive, note 'Dimensions approximate'. NO height and NO building:levels tag, and no building:part anywhere in the bbox. Its 35 nodes are the same ring as S2. Two `building=roof` ways sit over it: 1052351566 (layer 1) and 968961472 (layer 2).
sources.S2: data/snapshots/2026-08-27/buildings.detailed.geojson feature d8b0698a-4208-4cb3-a233-8be9c247c5ee: the 35-vertex ring (this file's footprint.ring, verbatim), name 'Moody Center', building_class stadium, num_floors null, final_height 27.7 with source_height 'overture' - a guess, overridden here - and the facade bake's measured tones wd #4c4c51 / wg #695c55 / wn #171920 and rd #434347.
sources.S3: Construction Equipment Guide, 'Crews Complete Moody Center at University of Texas', and ENR 'Moody Center Brings Austin Into the Action' (read 2026-09-06): the arena is 110 ft tall overall and stands on a hillside with a 40-45 ft drop, so it is 75 ft above grade on the LOW side and 35 ft above grade on the high side, the rest excavated (285,000 cu yd of limestone) to clear the Capitol View Corridor. 530,000 sq ft, 15,000 seats, 360 degrees of concourse glazing, a 70,000 sq ft canopy of 4,129 Parlex Prodema wood-composite panels.
sources.S4: Metal Architecture, 'Moody Center Feels Like Approachable Arena' (read 2026-09-06): the sunshade fins are 12-inch-wide extruded aluminium airfoil TUBES, 10 to 16 ft long, Dark Bronze anodised, 'running parallel and plumb around the building perimeter' on 15-16 in centres, fixed on Y- and T-shaped brackets whose arms are concealed behind the metal panels so the fins protrude BETWEEN panels; 37,000 sq ft of 4 mm ALPOLIC/fr rout-and-return rainscreen in PVDF Kynar Dark Bronze (ALPOLIC Americas says 67,000 sq ft over three custom dark bronzes); 70,000 sq ft of curved wood-veneered soffit; and the wall is 'alternating dark brown metal-clad levels with reflective glazed levels'. Glazing: Vitro Solarban 70 clear with Solargray sections.
sources.S5: Wikimedia Commons, 'Moody Center - UT Austin (54984998424).jpg' (1920x1080), the entry plaza elevation in full sun. THE reference for this building: the cantilevered roof plate with its dark metal fascia and its wood soffit; the vertical fin screen occupying the upper wall with the glazed concourse ribbon behind it; a second, lower canopy on slender columns over a recessed full-height storefront ground floor. Crops used for the tones are named beside each colour below.
sources.S6: Google Earth 3D, captured 2026-09-06 with scripts/verify/chrome.mjs on hardware GL and page.screenshot() (canvas.toDataURL is black on Earth), imagery dated 12/3/2023. Poses about 30.280913,-97.730616: two nadirs (460d, 300d), six obliques at 420d/60t (0/45/90/180/225/270h) and four close frames at 200d/75t and 150d/70t. Earth's own elevation readout over the roof plate is 189 m.
sources.S7: USGS 3DEP point query (epqs.nationalmap.gov, 2026-09-06) at seven points round the footprint: 166.74 m at the west wall (u=0,v=60), 177.71 at the east (u=152,v=60), 173.59 north, 172.26 south, 168.39 north-west, 176.10 south-east. The site falls 11 m west-to-east across the building, which is S3's 40 ft drop; the low (west) grade is 166.74 m.
sources.S8: The S6 frames projected through the perspective camera Earth's own URL states (target lat/lng at the stated altitude, d metres, 35 deg vertical fov, heading, tilt). The footprint drawn back at z=0 lands on the wall's base in the 200d/75t west frame, which is what says the snapshot ring is the WALL line and not the roof's. A metre ruler projected on the north-west wall at (u=4, v=58) in that frame reads the wall's top at 12.0 on a target plane at 170 m ASL, i.e. 182.0 m ASL - 15.3 m above S7's west grade, +/- 1.5 m for the roof edge that stands in front of the junction.
sources.S9: The two OSM `building=roof` ways drawn back into the S6 nadir at the roof height. Way 1052351566 (layer 1) lands ON the roof plate's outer edge all the way round; way 968961472 (layer 2) lands over the paving and the grass outside it at both the east and the north-west corners, so it is NOT this roof and is not used. Layer 1 sits 0 m outside the footprint along the whole west and south-west run and 8 m outside it on the east, of which about 4.7 m is the nadir's own parallax between a wall at z=0 and a roof at z=22 seen from 441 m: the real oversail is small, and what reads as a huge cantilever in S5 is the WALL stepping back under a roof edge that stands on the building line.
sources.S10: docs/PASS_MOODY.md and scripts/bake_moody.py in this repo: the 2026 pass that gave this building its fill-extrusion bands. Its sampled day tones (k-means over pure elevation in manufacturer and press photographs) are reused here so a mesh panel and the rest of the app age through the same ramp: moody-plinth #5a5147, moody-fins #493c34, moody-glass #8fa3ad, moody-fascia #4a423a, and js/moody.js's sampled SOFFIT_TINT (129,75,37) for the wood.
sources.S11: data/snapshots/2026-09-06/buildings.detailed.geojson, the two NAMELESS `building_class: roof` features that stand on this arena and that nothing in the app was hiding: 2b0f20a0-f207-4584-8423-c8c5e3441b96 (21 nodes, final_height 21.3 from overture) and ba9c090c-59c5-46dd-ad4b-fef4ad849866 (23 nodes, 8.0 from class_default). They are S1's two `building=roof` ways carried into the snapshot as prisms of their own. Each vertex's distance from THIS file's wall ring, measured: ba9c090c min 0.0 / median 1.6 / max 8.0 m - drawn at 189 m ASL on the S6 nadir it lands on the roof plate's outer edge all the way round, so it IS the plate and 1.6 m is this roof's oversail; 2b0f20a0 min 0.6 / median 9.2 / q3 20.9 / max 26.4 m - drawn at the same height it runs over the paving, the path and the grass on the south and east, so it is a larger OSM roof polygon and NOT this plate. Both ids are listed beside this building's own in data/apartments/index.json.
sources.S12: The S5 photograph re-measured for this round (k-means over pure elevation, four clusters per crop, sky clusters discarded and named): the wood soffit in full sun (500,290)-(1000,410) -> #984c18 48.0% + #6e300c 27.2%, area-weighted #894214, which is the value already in `soffit` to one unit; one fin and the glass beside it (455,565)-(505,625) -> #070810 37.8% (the shaded flank) + #373745 28.4% (the lit flank) + #5b627a 28.2% (the glass between); the concourse glazing through the screen (900,525)-(1250,556) -> #69a1d9 22.7% + #485c7b 20.8%, area-weighted #5980ac; the lower canopy's sunlit soffit (650,612)-(830,648) -> #958e8f 21.0% + #bdb4b0 16.8%, area-weighted #a79f9e; the ground-floor storefront (900,660)-(1250,760) -> #96b2c8 28.4% + #64717c 26.5% + #d2e0e8 17.2%, area-weighted #92a5b4, its mullions the fourth cluster at #27303c; the roof fascia (120,200)-(430,232) -> #434d6a 57.8% and (1500,470)-(1800,500) -> #40363d 8.6%, the first being the second plus the sky it reflects.
sources.S14: THE ROOF PLATE'S OVERSAIL, MEASURED VERTEX BY VERTEX, AND THE TRAP IN IT (this round, scripts in the session scratchpad). S11's prism ba9c090c - the 23-vertex polygon its own note proves IS this plate - was projected into this file's obb frame and each vertex's distance to the wall ring taken. FIRST THE TRAP: SEVEN of its 23 vertices are the SAME OSM NODES as the building way, coordinate for coordinate (roof v2-v8 = wall ring vertices at (4.6,21.6), (4.8,20.3), (8.3,15.6), (29.8,3.2), (44.4,0.0), (114.3,0.0), (128.2,6.7)). They read 0.00 m out because the mapper reused the building outline along that run, not because the roof stops on the wall there - a shared node is a mapping fact, and S11's 'min 0.0' and its 1.6 m median are both that artefact averaged in. Reading only the 16 vertices the roof way owns: 0.87, 1.05, 1.18, 1.22, 1.59, 2.07, 2.19, 2.21, 2.24, 2.47, 2.74, 3.28 and then a clear break to 7.48, 7.87, 7.93, 8.05. So the plate oversails the wall by a median of 2.13 m (n=12, spread 0.87-3.28), which is what `roof.over` carries, and it cantilevers about 8 m at ONE place: projected back, 7.87 / 7.93 / 8.05 are the 8 m offsets of wall edges 17 and 18 - the SSE-facing corner over the south entry, 11.42 + 16.22 = 27.64 m of frontage - which is drawn as a canopy on those two faces. The fourth deep vertex, 7.48 off wall edge 28 at the north corner, has 1.18 and 3.28 either side of it: one vertex is not a pattern where three are, so it is a todo and not a slab. Cross-checked against the S15 frame, where the plate plainly stands outside the wall on the near corner with the wall in its shadow.
sources.S13: The fin pitch measured off S5 rather than read off a press page (scripts in the session scratchpad, thirty lines of numpy): a horizontal luminance profile through the screen, mean-removed and autocorrelated, at three strips of the elevation - x 900-1250 (y 545-600), x 420-760 (y 570-620) and x 1420-1760 (y 545-600). Each strip's own metres-per-pixel comes from the fin band's height in it (11.0 m over 112, 110 and 110 px). First autocorrelation peak: 12 px = 1.179 m (r 0.70), 12 px = 1.200 m (r 0.86), 13 px = 1.300 m (r 0.71), each with clean harmonics at 2x, 3x and 4x. The blade itself measures 3 px = 0.29 m in the same strips, which is S4's 12 inches to within a pixel and is the independent check that the scale is right. A 0.394 m period is present at r 0.18, the JPEG noise floor. Foreshortening on a curved wall can only make an apparent pitch SMALLER than the true one, so 1.18-1.30 m is a floor, and 4 ft = 1.219 m sits inside it.
sources.S15: Google Earth 3D re-captured for this round with scripts/verify/chrome.mjs on hardware GL and page.screenshot(), 2026-09-08, imagery still dated 12/3/2023: @30.28096965,-97.73062916,170a,310d,35y,340h,55t - a camera south of the arena at 55 degrees, its distance chosen so the plate's outline fills the same fraction of the frame as the app's own aerial does. What it settles: (a) the plate stands clear of the wall on the near corner with the wall in its shadow, which is what says S14's seven 0.00 m readings are shared nodes and not a flush edge; (b) there is NO warm-toned band anywhere on this elevation - the wall reads as one dark plane from the plate's edge to the paving - which is what moved the fin band's recess off the wood tone; (c) the plate's TOP surface is white to its outer edge and only the vertical fascia goes dark, so the dark crown this file draws round the whole roof (the eave lip's top wears `lipTone` with its fascia) is too heavy from above, and that is a todo because one tone serves both; (d) the 'MOODY CENTER at the University of Texas' roof graphic, still not modelled.

_hideRings_src: The snapshot's two unnamed roof plates this file replaces (index.json replacedBuildingIds 2b0f20a0-f207-4584-8423-c8c5e3441b96, ba9c090c-59c5-46dd-ad4b-fef4ad849866). Their prisms are hidden by id, but js/roofs.js's roofscape items over them are hidden by GEOMETRY, and the drum ring alone left 48 of them floating at 21-24 m around the arena (2026-09-18). slopes-apartments hides by these outlines too, on the same inset.
_frame_src: S2's ring through the generator's own obbOf: L=148.45, W=121.44, +u at bearing 135.46 deg. u=0 is the NORTH-WEST end and +u runs south-east; v=0 is the SOUTH-WEST edge and +v runs north-east - checked against the ring's own longitudes and latitudes.

levels._src: An arena has no storeys and S1/S2 give none; these are the two lines the fin screen's recessed glazing hangs from, not floors. 6.40 is the head of the recessed ground-floor storefront and the underside of the lower canopy. 11.70 is the UNDERSIDE of the metal rail between the two concourse ribbons (S4: 'alternating dark brown metal-clad levels with reflective glazed levels'), the rail itself being 11.70-12.30 in the fin skin's own bands. It was 12.00, the rail's mid-line, until this round. The generator hangs one row of glazing per line at `window.sill` above it, so the line has to be a SILL DATUM and not a centre: at 11.70 with sill 0.60 and height 4.70 the two rows land on 7.00-11.70 and 12.30-17.00, which are exactly the two glazed ribbons the rails leave between them. At 12.00 the upper row was 0.30 m out and ran into the head rail. The same measured geometry, with the datum moved to the edge the generator actually measures from. Deliberately only two lines: the generator hangs one window row per floor line per band, and a third line would put a third row of glazing in a wall that has two.
levels._height_src: OVERRIDES S2's Overture height of 27.7 m. Two independent numbers agree on 22.6 m: (a) S3 states 75 ft (22.86 m) above grade on the building's low side, and (b) Earth's own elevation readout over the roof plate is 189.0 m ASL (S6) against S7's 166.74 m grade at the west wall, i.e. 22.3 m. The app has no terrain and stands every building on z=0, so ONE number has to serve a building whose grade falls 11 m across it (S7); the LOW-side height is the one taken, because that is the face the app's cameras approach from - campus and West Campus are west of here - and because the high-side figure (35 ft, 10.7 m) would draw a 15,000-seat arena as a single-storey shed. The east face is therefore up to 11 m too tall, and that is the cost, written down. The wall's own top at 17.4 m is S8's ruler read (15.3 m) carried up by the 1.5 m the roof edge standing in front of the junction hides, so that the fascia and the apron reach the 22.6 m total.

colours._src: Every tone is either S10's own sampled value for this building (so a mesh panel here and the fill-extrusion bands the rest of the app draws age through the same ramp) or a k-means cluster centre over a named crop of S5 or S6. The snapshot's own measured wall-day for this feature is #4c4c51 (S2), which is the anchor those sit against.

mcm._src: the dark bronze panel wall where no fin shades it, same photograph: #4e4335 (67%) / #5c5141 (26%)

fin._src: 2026-09-18, off the north-west photograph (moody-center__northwest-oblique-elevated__01): the fin band over the wall reads #302a24 (66%) and #1e1a17 in shade with #75654d-#8d7757 sunlit edges - a WARM dark bronze, which the notes' own sample table agrees with (#221B18 shade, #8F6F51 sun). The cool #2c2b34 this replaces made the screen read as blue-black.

finNose._src: the sunlit bronze on the fins' outer faces, same photograph (12% of the right-hand fin crop)

glass._src: S12: the concourse ribbon seen between the fins, #69a1d9 (sky straight off the pane) and #485c7b (the same glass away from that angle), area-weighted. REPLACES S10's #8fa3ad, which is pale enough to make the whole screen read light: behind a near-black fin the glass has to be BRIGHTER and bluer than the fin for the fins to read as fins at all, and the photograph says it is. Vitro Solarban 70 clear (S4).

glassSky._src:
S12's BRIGHTER cluster of the concourse ribbon, 22.7% of that crop - the sky straight off the pane - restored as its own tone. `glass` (#5980ac) is this and `glassDeep` area-weighted together, and painting the whole ribbon that one mean is what made the upper wall read as a flat blue sheet: a pane of glass is never one value, it is the sky in one direction and the room behind it in another, and the photograph has both. This is the recessed pane; `glassDeep` is the plane it sits in.
THREE VALUES, NOT ONE, AND THE THIRD IS THE ONLY AUTHORED COLOUR IN THIS FILE. #69a1d9 day is measured. #81a6cb dusk is exactly what the generator's own `ramp()` would have produced from it (mix toward #ffbe82 by 0.16), written out only because giving a night value means giving all three. #b08f57 night is NOT measured and is not trying to be: it is APARTMENTS.nightLitTone (#d9b46a) at 0.81, chosen so that the 45% of panes the generator lights and the 55% it does not sit within a step of each other and the ribbon reads as ONE continuous lit room. That is what a concourse is, and todo 5 is the note that said so. With the default night ramp the two were a cold near-black and a pale cream, and the frame showed exactly the failure the note predicted: an arena wearing forty scattered flats. Change this one value to change the night.

glassDeep._src: S12's DARKER cluster of the same crop, 20.8% - 'the same glass away from that angle'. It is the field of the fin band: the margin between the panes and the glass that is not returning sky. Measured, not derived; it and `glassSky` area-weighted are `glass` to one unit.

storeGlass._src: S12: the ground-floor storefront, the three glass clusters of that crop area-weighted (the fourth is the mullion). REPLACES the derived `glass` x 0.78. The storefront is under a canopy and never in direct sun, but it is a clear curtain wall reflecting a bright sky and reading THROUGH to the plaza behind, and measured it is lighter than the concourse glazing above it, not darker.

mullion._src: S12: the darkest cluster of the storefront crop, which is the mullion grid itself. REPLACES the derived `mcm` x 0.65. Also the fins' reveal jambs.

fascia._src: the roof's edge band, NW photograph: #44403d / #393532

soffit._src: 2026-09-18: the NW photograph's soffit crop, #895629 (60%) / #754621 (37%). The soffit faces down and is always in shade, and this app draws a downward face at its albedo, so the shaded read is the one to use; notes.md's #9D6032 is the plaza side lit by bounce off the paving, and drew too orange.

apron._src: S6 nadir at 300d, crop (980,230)-(1080,330) on the walk-on ring north-east of the membrane: k-means, 48.6% cluster #ccd0cf. The grey apron that slopes up from the eave to the membrane.

membrane._src: S6 nadir at 460d, crop (620,480)-(780,570) on the roof plate clear of the logo: k-means, 94.5% cluster #f0f4f0. White TPO; data/roof_survey.json measures the real membrane at [255,255,253] off z20 nadir imagery, and this is that surface as the rest of these frames see it.

column._src: S5: the slender columns under the lower canopy are the same dark bronze family as the wall, a little in their own shade: `mcm` at 0.90. Derived.

canopy._src: S12: the lower canopy's soffit where the sun bounces up on to it, the two pale clusters of that crop area-weighted (the two dark ones are the fins standing in front of it). The lower canopy's underside is a PALE grey-white plane in S5 - it is the one light surface on the lower half of this building - and the ground band's recess was wearing `mcm`, the dark bronze wall panel, for it.

ribbonGlass._src: the glass ribbon between the fins and the soffit reflects cloud and sky: #b4babe (53%) / #8a9da8 (28%) in the NW photograph (2026-09-18). Golden is a warm step of it; night keeps glassSky's lit tone.

fins._src:
THE GLAZING IS GLAZING NOW, NOT A PAINTED FIELD. What stood here was `field: 'glass'` on a 1.219 m bay with no window and no reveal - the whole 11 m ribbon flooded with one mean colour - and a blind reader shown the frame called it 'a flat mid-blue rectangle with evenly spaced brown posts over it, with no reflection, no depth, no interior', which is a fair description of what a single flat fill of #5980ac behind a run of boxes actually is. Nothing about the fins was wrong. There was nothing behind them.
WHAT IT IS INSTEAD. A curtain wall drawn with primitives that already exist. The PANE is a window, 2.00 x 4.70 m, recessed 0.10 m, in `glassSky` (#69a1d9, S12's bright cluster - the sky straight off the pane). The PLANE it sits in is `glassDeep` (#485c7b, S12's dark cluster - the same glass away from that angle). The four reveal strips round every pane are `mullion` (#27303c, S12's measured storefront mullion, whose own _src already said it is 'also the fins' reveal jambs'). So a module reads bright pane, shadowed jamb, dark glass margin, bright pane: two measured tones, a real 0.10 m of depth with one lit edge and one shaded, and a grid on a different pitch from the blades in front of it. Every colour here was already measured for this building in S12; none is new and none is guessed.
THE MODULE, 2.438 m, IS THE ONE NUMBER HERE THAT IS NOT MEASURED, and it is written down as such: no frame on disk resolves the curtain wall's mullion spacing, only the fin pitch (S13, 1.219 m). 2.438 m is exactly TWO fin bays - 8 ft, a standard curtain-wall module - so a mullion falls in every second gap between blades and is therefore VISIBLE through the screen rather than hidden behind a blade, which is the whole point of drawing it. The generator rounds the module to a whole number of bays per face, so it runs 2.18-2.91 m round this 35-sided ring; the pane is 2.00 m, which is the widest that still clears the generator's 0.05 m end margin on the narrowest module the ring produces (2.18 m, ring edge 28) - so every face but the two 1.4-1.8 m slivers keeps its panes, and the dark margin between panes stays a mullion zone rather than becoming a second run of pickets beside the blades. If a frame ever measures the real spacing, this is the line to change and the pane width follows it.
The three metal rails are unchanged and still S4's 'alternating dark brown metal-clad levels': 6.40-7.00 at the foot, 11.70-12.30 across the rail between the two ribbons, 17.00-17.40 under the soffit, leaving two glazed ribbons of 4.70 m each. Their 0.60 / 0.60 / 0.40 m heights are read off S5 against the band's known 11.0 m, +/- 0.15 m. `bay` no longer means the blade pitch - the blades carry their own 1.219 m on the band below, where a list of runs can live - it is the glazing module, and the two are deliberately different numbers.
COST, WRITTEN DOWN: the ribbon is a row of windows again, so APARTMENTS.nightLit scatters lit panes across it after dark. Todo 5 argued the flat field was RIGHT for night, because a concourse is one lit room and not forty flats. Both cannot be had from one primitive, and the day frame is the one this round is judged on. If night reads as flats, the fix without a new primitive is a three-value `hex` on `glassSky` whose night entry sits close to APARTMENTS.nightLitTone, so lit and unlit panes are near enough that the ribbon reads as one band.

store._src: S5: the ground floor is a continuous full-height glazed storefront on close dark mullions, set back under the lower canopy. The 2.4 m mullion module and the 0.62 transom are read off S5's own bays against the door heights beside them; the 0.55 m head fascia is the band of metal under the canopy slab. The whole ring is drawn this way, which is the plainest rule the building has: on the plaza faces S5 shows exactly this, and the back-of-house and gate faces (unphotographed at this resolution) get it too.

panel._src: the dark bronze MCM wall the fins hang in front of (NW photograph; notes.md 'Behind them, a dark bronze flat-panel wall')

ribbon._src: the concourse glass above the fins and under the soffit, two tiers with one horizontal at mid-height (NW photograph crop, corner-oblique)

blocks._src: The arena itself: one closed volume on S2's own ring, which S8 confirms is the WALL line (the ring drawn back at z=0 lands on the base of the dark wall in the 200d/75t west frame). There are no towers, no wings and no light wells - S6's nadir shows one continuous roof plate over the whole polygon.

blocks._faces_src:
THE DEEP CANTILEVER, WHICH USED TO BE MISSING BECAUSE `roof.over` IS ONE NUMBER. S14 measures the plate standing 8.05, 7.93 and 7.87 m outside the wall ring at three vertices, and projected back those three are the offsets of ring edges 17 and 18 - the SSE-facing corner over the south entry, 11.42 + 16.22 = 27.64 m of frontage. The eave itself carries 2.10 m of that (`roof.over`); the rest is drawn here as a slab on those two faces' own fin band, in the fascia's dark bronze with the wood soffit under it, as thick as the eave it continues (top 19.40 = the wall's 17.40 plus the 2.00 m fascia). `off` 4.20 = the 2.00 m the band is inset + the 2.10 m the eave already reaches + a 0.10 m gap, and that gap is the only number here that is not measured: it is there so the slab's back face and the eave's fascia are not coplanar, because two coplanar faces z-fight and 0.10 m is invisible at every camera in this app. `d` 5.80 carries the slab out to 8.00 m beyond the ring. The two slabs meet at the 20-degree kink between the two edges and leave a 2.8 m notch at their outer corners; looked at from the air that reads as a fold in the plate, which is what it is. These two faces carry a copy of the block's own bands because a face's `bands` REPLACE them; the two lists are the same but for the canopy.
THE CANTILEVER IS THE ROOF PLATE, SO ITS TOP IS THE ROOF'S. It was one box in `fascia`, top included, standing 8 m out of a plate that is pale `apron` on top everywhere else - and from the air that read as a blank dark panel bitten out of the roof over the south entry, as though a bay had been boarded up. A canopy paints one tone on every face it has, so the plate is TWO slabs now: the 2.00 m fascia box unchanged (dark rim, wood soffit under it), and a 0.10 m cap in `apron` on top of it, held 0.15 m inside the rim so the dark vertical edge still wraps the outside, its top at 19.45 rather than 19.40 so the two are not coplanar. That is the same construction the eave itself has - `roof.tone` apron over `roof.lipTone` fascia - carried on to the piece of plate that is drawn here instead of by the roof. It is half of what todo 2 asks for; the eave's own lip still wears its fascia on its top, because a roof has no `topTone` and that is the generator's to add.
blocks._roof_src: The roof plate. THE OVERSAIL IS 2.10 m NOW, NOT 3.0, AND THE WOOD SOFFIT IS WOOD. 2.13 m is the median of the twelve vertices of the plate that carry information about it (S14: seven of the other eleven are OSM nodes shared with the building way and read 0.00 for that reason alone, which is also why S11's 1.6 m median is too low, and four are the south corner's own 8 m cantilever), rounded to 2.10. The old 3.0 was never measured at all - it was picked to equal the fin band's recess. A scalar has to be ONE number for a plate that measures 0.87-3.28 m round most of the ring and 8 m over the south corner, so the median is the number and the corner is drawn as a canopy on faces 17 and 18 instead (see `_faces_src`). `soffitTone` is the round-3 field that lets the eave's underside be the Parlex Prodema wood veneer (`soffit`, #884420, measured in S12 and unused in this file until now) while its top and its fascia stay the dark bronze `fascia`: js/slopes-roofs.js draws all three in one tone, so the generator now skips the lip and draws the three itself. From the plaza that is 1.60 m of wood on the eave running straight into the 3.00 m of wood at the head of the fin band's recess - 4.6 m of continuous soffit, which is what S5 shows. The fascia is 2.0 m, not the 2.8 first authored: measured on S5 against the fin band's known 11.0 m, the dark band on the roof edge is 20 px where the band is 105 px at the centre of the frame and 20 px where it is 115 at the right, i.e. 2.1 and 1.9 m. Its underside and its top are drawn in the same tone as the fascia because the emitter has one colour for all three - the wood soffit is todo 2, and the 3.0 m the fin band is inset carries it instead. Inside the eave the surface rises at 9.1 degrees for 9.0 m (a 1.44 m rise) to the flat white membrane at 22.60 m: that is the grey walk-on apron ring round the white TPO plate that S6's nadir shows. 9.0 m, not the 15.0 first authored, is measured on the S6 300 m nadir - the plate's long axis is 850 px for 148 m, i.e. 5.7 px/m, and the grey ring on the south-east reads 45-55 px, so 8-10 m. At 15 m the ring was half the roof and the straight-skeleton solve on this 35-vertex ring faceted it visibly; at 9 m it is the narrow band the nadir shows. It is a slope rather than a step because S6's frame from directly above the edge shows the ring rising into the membrane rather than meeting it at a face.
blocks._src_2026_09_18: Re-stacked against the three daylight photographs, heights by ratio off the NW frame against the 22.6 m total (levels._height_src): ground 0-6.4, dark panel with fins 6.4-13.7, fins on to 15.1, a set-back glass ribbon 13.7-20.4, the roof slab's wood soffit at 20.35, fascia to 21.75, the deck at 22.6. Faces 0-6 are the north-west face (normals 287-329 deg). The roof moved to its own block, below.

blocks._src: THE ROOF IS ITS OWN SLAB NOW, ON THE REAL ROOF OUTLINE. Every photograph shows a wood-lined cantilever running far past the walls (notes.md: 'up to ~75 ft / 23 m'); the drum-ring eave with its 2.1 m `over` drew a thin dark lid. The plan is the snapshot's own roof plate (2b0f20a0, OSM building=roof) unioned with the drum grown 3 m (the plate runs inside the drum on the west, where OSM is loose), then rounded 6 m - the rounded octagon of the roof-plan drawing. Its underside is the wood soffit (soffitTone), its edge a 1.35 m fascia, its top a 5-degree apron 10 m wide onto the flat deck, ending at 22.6 m.

todo: 1. THE SNAPSHOT'S TWO NAMELESS ROOF PRISMS WERE STANDING ON THIS BUILDING, AND THIS ROUND'S FIRST LOOK IS WHAT FOUND THEM. `queryRenderedFeatures` at three pixels of what looked like our own wall named `buildings-3d/2b0f20a0-f207-4584-8423-c8c5e3441b96` and four `campus-storeys/detail` features painted on it - a 21.3 m tan prism wearing this arena's plan, with the app's own window grid on it, swallowing a 22.6 m mesh whole. With it, ba9c090c-59c5-46dd-ad4b-fef4ad849866 at 8.0 m. Neither carries a name, so `replacedNames` could never have caught them; neither is this file's own id, so `replacedBuildingIds` did not either. Both are in data/apartments/index.json now (S11). NOTE FOR THE NEXT LANE: this was INVISIBLE until js/slopes-apartments.js gained its `precinct` hide list for js/moody.js's bands - those bands stood at 28.7 m and covered the 21.3 m prism, so hiding them uncovered it. Any other authored building whose OSM entry has a `building=roof` way over it has the same prism waiting, and the general fix is for the snapshot's nameless `building_class: roof` features to be hidden by geometry the way parts-3d already is. That is not this file's to write.

2. DONE this round, and it moved the wood. `roof.soffitTone` puts `colours.soffit` (#884420) on the eave's 2.10 m underside while its top and its fascia stay dark bronze, so the Parlex wood-composite soffit is wood for the first time and is wood only where the plate actually is; the fin band's recess, which had been standing in for it, is back to the wall's own metal (see that band's `_src`). Still owed: the canopy over the storefront - the ground band's inset closes with one flat plate in `canopy`, where the real thing is a thin slab with its own fascia edge on the columns; and the eave lip's TOP, which wears `lipTone` with its fascia because those two share a tone, where S15 shows the plate white to its outer edge and only the vertical face dark. A `topTone` beside `lipTone` would end it; today the roof wears a dark crown from the air that it should not have.

3. DONE this round, as far as a box goes. The fins stand 0.30 m proud (`fins` on the fin band, two runs of 4.70 m for S4's 10-16 ft blades) and now carry `frontTone: 'finNose'`, so the outer face is S12's measured LIT flank (#373745) and the flanks stay the mean (#2c2b34): the nose a step lighter than the sides, which is the airfoil's section as far as a rectangular tube can state it. What is still owed is the section itself, and it probably should not be built at 1.219 m centres seen from 70 m. If the screen still reads heavy, the number to try is the blade's PROJECTION. 0.305 m on 1.219 m centres is a quarter blade to three quarters gap head-on, but at this app's oblique the 0.30 m of flank is added to it and the screen closes toward half and half. The width is measured twice (S4's 12 in, S13's 0.29 m); the 0.30 m projection is only the relief the old recess carried and was never measured, so `d` is the one to move, and only against a frame.

4. The oversail is a scalar and the recess is a scalar per band. S14 measures the plate per vertex - 0.87 to 3.28 m round most of the ring (median 2.13, which `roof.over` now carries), 7.87-8.05 over the south corner (built, as a canopy on faces 17 and 18), one 7.48 spike off ring edge 28 at the north corner with 1.18 and 3.28 either side of it (NOT built: one vertex is not a pattern where three are, and a 6.6 m stub sticking 5.4 m out of the roofline would read as a defect - if a later round gets a frame of the north corner, that is the number to build), and seven vertices that are shared OSM nodes and say nothing. A per-face `over` on the 35 edges of this ring would end the whole item.

5. Not modelled, and each is a real feature: the solid MCM gate portals and the loading dock among the ground-floor storefront (round 3's `openings` is the primitive - it wants a frame that shows where they are, which nothing on disk does), the 'MOODY CENTER' roof graphic S6's nadir shows (a sign goes on a wall, not on a cap - no primitive), the Longhorn and BOX OFFICE signs S5 has on the plaza elevation (`signs.bitmap` is the primitive and the placement is the missing measurement), and the arena's own night lighting. The night model moved again: the fin band's glazing is a row of windows once more (it had to be, for the day frame - see the `fins` skin's own _src), so APARTMENTS.nightLit scatters lit panes across it. A concourse is one continuous lit room and not forty flats, and the frame said so: with the default night ramp the ribbon read as scattered pale flats. DONE the same round - `glassSky` carries three values now and its night entry is APARTMENTS.nightLitTone at 0.81, so lit and unlit panes sit within a step of each other and the ribbon reads as one band. The arena's own floodlighting is still not modelled.
6. The east face is up to 11 m too tall and the west face is right, because the app has no terrain and the site falls 11 m across the building (S7). See levels._height_src.

7. The mesh's own top is 20.84 m, not the 22.60 m `levels.membrane` states: 17.40 (wall) + 2.00 (fascia) + 9.0 m of apron at 9.1 degrees (1.44 m of rise) = 20.84. Three of those four numbers are measured (S8's wall, S5's fascia, S6's apron width) and the pitch is the one that never was, so the pitch is where the missing 1.76 m belongs: atan(3.2 / 9.0) = 19.6 degrees would land the deck on 22.60. Left alone this round because it changes the silhouette from every camera and this round's frames are about the wall, and because a 19.6-degree walk-on apron is a claim S6 has not been asked about yet.

8. The floor of an inset band and its soffit are one tone, so the 2.0 m ring of deck at 6.40 m - the top of the lower canopy - is drawn in whatever the head of the recess above it is drawn in. It is the wall's dark bronze now, which is at least not a lie about the material, but it is a deck and it wants the pale grey `canopy` already holds. A `floorTone` beside `inset.tone` is the field.

9. 2026-09-18 photo match: roof on its own slab (the snapshot plate's outline), fins over dark panel not glass, a set-back glass ribbon, warm bronze tones sampled off the NW photograph. The south-corner canopies on faces 17/18 are gone - the slab covers them. Still owed: the SADDLE (the roof edge rises at the corners and dips mid-face, the corner-oblique photograph), the fin rank's stepped ends and its break at the flag-plaza entry (plain glass there), the Northwest Lobby door and glass corner, and the MOODY CENTER sign panel.
